Claude Code instances in parallel if you
wanna work on multiple tasks at the same

But here I'll start with one simple task,

project, and I tell it to not implement

And then I'll switch to plan mode. Plan mode
is another mode supported by Claude Code,
and you switch between modes by hitting
Shift+Tab.
And here's a simple recommendation. For the
vast majority of tasks, you should start in
plan mode, even if they seem simple.
Plan mode is a mode where Claude Code will
first gather some relevant information
before starting work,
and it will ask you for clarification
questions if more clarification is needed.
It can help you turn
average prompts into good prompts,
essentially.
And it allows you to
be a bit more lazy, though ideally you're
not lazy, but you're turning good prompts
into amazing prompts.
Either way,
using plan mode is a pretty good default and
indeed my default for most prompts I send to
Claude Code. If you send a task in plan mode
to Claude Code, it can't edit files. Files
yet. It doesn't have the permissions for
that yet when using that mode. Instead, it
starts by exploring your project and by then
creating a plan on how to tackle the task
you gave it. And it may also ask for further
clarification
depending on your prompt and the task you
gave it. It also saves those plans locally
temporarily so that it always has access to
them, even in situations where your context
window should clutter up and needs to be
cleared, even then it would still be able to
refer back to that plan. But we'll get back
to full context windows a little bit later.

made. So here it describes which routes it
wants to set up
and it then gives you more details here
and then gives you a couple of options. It
may also ask some questions here depending
on how well written your prompt was, how
complex the task was, and simply also some
randomness.
